purpose: Closed protocol-major-1 contract for the bundled pinned rustc_driver semantic sidecar. It composes exact C-2 stage input, RESOLVED-INPUTS rust-v1 identity, a sealed Snapshot VFS, FACT-PLANE candidates, complete Coverage and conditional D9 fate without inheriting the TypeScript wire contract.

dependencyPins.selector: ExecutionPlan fact-derivation stages, StageBudgetV1 and CoverageKey
candidate code maps and termination semantics

canonicalCbor.mapOrder: Sort keys first by byte length of the deterministic-CBOR encoded text key, then lexicographically by those unsigned encoded bytes for equal lengths.
canonicalCbor.decodeRule: Retain the original payload bytes, reject duplicate/noncanonical input before semantic decoding, decode exactly once under the frame's closed payload schema, re-encode and require byte-for-byte equality. Missing, unknown, mistyped, out-of-range or contradictory values are provider-protocol; no ignore-unknown, coercion, float conversion or last-key-wins behavior exists.

framing.frameBytes: exactly uint64-big-endian payloadLength, then 32 raw SHA-256 digest bytes, then payloadLength canonical-CBOR payload bytes
framing.lengthScope: payload bytes only; it excludes the 8-byte length and 32-byte digest
framing.digestScope: SHA-256 of the exact canonical-CBOR payload bytes only
framing.allocationRule: Read exactly 8 length bytes and reject a value above maxFramePayloadBytes before payload allocation; read exactly 32 digest bytes; then read exactly payloadLength bytes with cumulative overflow checks.
framing.stdoutRule: stdout is protocol-only from child start through EOF. Any non-frame byte, diagnostic text, prefix truncation, payload truncation, digest mismatch, noncanonical payload or byte after a terminal is provider-protocol.
framing.eofRule: EOF is valid only after one valid terminal, observed child exit status zero and no extra stdout byte. EOF before a terminal or before the required process-fate checks is provider-protocol.
framing.extraRule: A complete second prefix, partial prefix, whitespace, BOM, log byte or any other stdout byte after terminal is provider-protocol.

limits.limitRule: Reject a declared size/count above its bound before allocation or append. Sum payload, file, candidate and spool sizes with checked uint64 arithmetic. Safety bounds are not semantic budgets; a safety-bound or supervisor-deadline failure cannot manufacture BudgetExhausted.

schemaLanguage.maps: Every named payload/definition with closed=true has exactly its required fields, no optional fields unless explicitly listed, and no additional properties. A nullable field is present with null; omission is not null.
schemaLanguage.arrays: Definite arrays preserve order unless the field declares canonical sorted-unique order. Bounds are inclusive.
schemaLanguage.integer: Exact mathematical nonnegative integer encoded as CBOR major type 0; booleans are not integers; every integer is within its declared inclusive range.
schemaLanguage.text: Exact UTF-8 NFC text satisfying the declared byte bound, pattern, enum or equality; no coercion.
schemaLanguage.bytes: Exact CBOR byte string satisfying the declared bound; JSON conformance vectors transcribe it as lowercase even-length hex outside the wire schema.
schemaLanguage.external: An external type is recursively validated against the exact dependency bytes and selector pinned above; owner booleans, producer field presence or a precomputed digest never replace recursive validation.
schemaLanguage.union: Variant selection is by the named tag and every variant has one exact field set.

ProtocolLimitsV1.rule: Every value is uint64 and exactly equals this artifact's limits object.

requestProjection.identity: Hello expected identity is copied from the verified signed release plus the exact rust-v1 Plan value. OpenUniverse carries the complete rust-v1 value, never a digest-only substitute.
requestProjection.stage: Analyze stages are copied exactly from the verified C-2 ExecutionPlan selection rule, with absent optional arrays represented as empty and absent budget represented as null. The host adds only the sealed subject manifest and complete requested Coverage domain under the exact rules above.
requestProjection.snapshot: The host sends one complete manifest sorted by CanonicalPath, then every file's non-empty chunks in manifest/path order and contiguous chunk order, then one seal. Symlinks carry target bytes in the manifest and no chunk. No live root, file descriptor, host path, lazy read callback or provider filesystem lookup is an input authority.
requestProjection.repositoryResolution: The exact disabled/prepared value is derived from the narrow RI join. Prepared outputs already entered PlanId; the semantic child only validates and consumes them.
requestProjection.sourceDisclosure: No SnapshotManifest or SnapshotFileChunk may be sent until HelloAck identity and capabilities are recursively equal to expected signed/Plan values and UniverseAccepted exactly echoes the complete OpenUniverse value.

responseProjection.candidate: Every FactBatch candidate is candidate-only. The host recursively validates FACT-PLANE relation, rung, layer, producer, version, language, universes, confidence, relation schema, canonical relation-payload bytes and anchors against the admitted stage/snapshot before spooling. The provider never mints FACT-ID.
responseProjection.coverage: Every successful stage emits exactly one Coverage after its zero or more contiguous FactBatch frames. Coverage entries form a bijection with the stage's requestedCoverageDomain in the exact request order and are all complete/null-deficiency. Unavailable and BudgetExhausted carry the exhaustive stage-major domain as unknown with their one canonical deficiency.
responseProjection.terminal: Complete, Unavailable, BudgetExhausted, ProviderFault and Cancelled are the only worker terminals. A terminal is candidate output until zero exit and EOF are verified. Cancel is the sole host terminal transition and authorizes only Cancelled.
responseProjection.typedFault: ProviderFault is a closed diagnostic terminal that always maps to provider-protocol; its detailCode never becomes a public D9 code.

commitments.emptyRule: An empty candidate stream is the deterministic-CBOR empty array under the applicable domain and is never omitted. A requested Coverage domain is never empty.

orderingAndStateMachine.sequenceRule: Each direction has an independent uint64 sequence beginning at zero and increasing by exactly one for every frame. Duplicate, skipped, decreasing, overflowing or replayed sequence is provider-protocol. There is no retransmission, retry acknowledgement or deduplication state in v1.
orderingAndStateMachine.stageOrder: Analyze stage order. For each stage, zero or more FactBatch frames with batchIndex 0..n-1 and contiguous candidateOrdinal values are followed by exactly one Coverage before a later stage emits anything.
orderingAndStateMachine.unavailableRule: Unavailable is valid only as the first worker analysis output immediately after Analyze and before every FactBatch or Coverage.
orderingAndStateMachine.budgetRule: BudgetExhausted may occur during analysis only for a non-milliseconds requested stage budget. All prior candidates remain candidate-only and are discarded.
orderingAndStateMachine.cancelRule: The host may send Cancel exactly once from any nonterminal state, then closes its request side. Only Cancelled may follow. On the host user signal path, a forced kill or missing Cancelled during bounded cleanup does not overwrite D9 interrupted precedence.
orderingAndStateMachine.terminalRule: After any worker terminal no protocol frame or stdout byte is permitted. Valid Complete, Unavailable, BudgetExhausted, ProviderFault or Cancelled must be followed by exit status zero within normalExitGraceMilliseconds and then EOF. Any nonzero exit, signal death, timeout, extra byte or missing EOF is provider-protocol, except host user-signal cleanup retains interrupted precedence.
orderingAndStateMachine.unknownRule: Any transition not enumerated or refined by the stage/cancel rules, any second terminal, any second Analyze, or any payload contradicting retained session state is provider-protocol.

deterministicBudget.milliseconds: A C-2 milliseconds budget is a host supervisor deadline only. It is transmitted for exact projection but cannot authorize BudgetExhausted; expiry is an incomplete child protocol and maps provider-protocol unless a user signal has precedence.
deterministicBudget.work-units: Increment once before examining each canonical tuple (stage, subjectOrdinal, requestedCoverageDomain entryOrdinal); the first tuple whose increment would exceed limit yields observed=limit+1.
deterministicBudget.items: Increment once before staging each FactCandidateV1; the first candidate whose increment would exceed limit yields observed=limit+1.
deterministicBudget.bytes: Increment by the exact canonical-CBOR byte length of each candidate before staging it; the first candidate that would make the checked sum exceed limit yields observed=limit+1 only when the increment is one, otherwise observed is the exact first disallowed checked sum.
deterministicBudget.overflow: Counter overflow is provider-protocol, never BudgetExhausted.

candidateAtomicity.spoolBound: maxCandidateSpoolBytes and maxFactCandidatesTotal across the complete Analyze
admitOn: all frame digests and canonical-CBOR schemas valid
stage, batch and candidate ordering exact
every FactCandidateV1 recursively valid against FACT-PLANE and host context
every requested Coverage domain has an exact complete bijection
all stage and stream commitments recompute
EOF follows with no extra byte
candidateAtomicity.admission: After every condition succeeds, atomically admit the complete Analyze candidate set through the host FACT-PLANE boundary and admit its complete Coverage. Failure of any condition admits neither a candidate nor partial Coverage.
discardAllOn: protocol, identity, schema, sequence, commitment, candidate or Coverage fault
spool, frame, request, response, scratch or count bound
candidateAtomicity.unavailableAndBudgetCoverage: Only after a valid terminal, exhaustive unknown Coverage commitment, zero exit and EOF may the host admit the terminal's Coverage; all fact candidates remain discarded.

repositoryExecution.default: disabled; no build scripts, procedural macros, compiler plugins or project hooks execute; generated-cfg-dependent domains return valid Unavailable/provider-unavailable
repositoryExecution.preparedGrant: The host resolved-inputs adapter, not the semantic child, owns a per-project network=false pre-Plan preparation. Exact tool paths are carried in capabilityGrant parameters and exact outputs in rust-v1; both enter PlanId before this child starts.
repositoryExecution.semanticChild: Consumes the sealed prepared outputs and tool-path identity only. It cannot execute project code, fetch packages, choose a substitute tool, modify the outputs or expand the grant.
repositoryExecution.pluginsAndHooks: compiler plugins and project hooks are forbidden in both variants
repositoryExecution.inheritance: A grant is exact to one projectId and never global or inherited by another Plan/Project.

d9Join.rule: Use no private public code. This candidate reference does not integrate v1.13 into DELIVERY or supersede DELIVERY's currently bound v1.6.

conformanceCorpus.checkerRule: The retained checker must hash dependencies before semantic use, cross-read both joins, strictly parse JSON, recursively validate exact types, remain total on malformed values, refuse a dirty selftest base, count a failed mutation application as an escape and reject every listed fork.

residuals: This protocol and both narrow joins require independent review and formal application; they are not current DELIVERY/RI integration authority.
D9 v1.13 remains candidate-not-applied despite its independent pre-freeze review.
No Rust host, rustc_driver child, repository-resolution adapter, corpus run, platform qualification or release evidence is supplied by this architecture contract.
The exact upstream allocation recipe for ExecutionId is outside this protocol; the wire carries and compares the host's already-allocated canonical nonempty value without deriving it.
